name: letter-of-rec-drafter
description: Drafts a recommendation letter from your actual notes and memories of the person, in your letter voice, shaped to the specific opportunity — and refuses to invent accomplishments you didn't give it evidence for. On first run it learns your letter voice from a past letter or two you're proud of. Then you hand it the raw material — what you genuinely remember, their CV or résumé, the job or program they're applying to — and it drafts a voice-true letter, flags any claim it couldn't ground in your evidence, and produces the length you need: full letter, short form, or a portal text-box paragraph. Missing evidence comes back as a question, never as filler. Use during recommendation-letter season or any time someone asks you for a reference. Trigger phrases include "write a rec letter", "letter of recommendation", "a student asked me for a reference", "draft a LOR", "recommendation for grad school", "reference letter for a colleague", "I need to write a rec for".
